rounds.rule: Start with the ball in the middle and a hidden orientation normal. Shake toggles the orientation; tilt left moves the ball one place left if normal and one place right if toggled, tilt right moves it one place right if normal and one place left if toggled, and the ball stops at the ends.

commitments.why: If it did not end right, the idea that a shake reverses left tilts, so repeated left tilts push the ball right, would be wrong.
If it did not end left, the symmetric claim that a shake reverses right tilts, so repeated right tilts push the ball left, would be wrong.
If it ended left, it would suggest shake does not flip the tilt direction or does not toggle back after two shakes.
If it ended right, it would cast doubt on shake toggling orientation for right tilts.
If it ended middle, it would contradict that after a shake a right tilt pushes left from the left end.

rounds.rule: The ball starts in the middle. Tilt left/right normally move it one place left/right, but each shake toggles a hidden parity so that until the next shake, tilts are reversed; the ball stops at the ends.

commitments.why: A rule without shake-reversal would predict left, so right is a strong test of the hidden parity.
A rule without shake-reversal would predict right, so left is a strong test of the hidden parity.
If it came out right, the second shake would not be restoring the original tilt direction; this tests that shakes toggle parity rather than permanently reversing it.
If it came out right, tilt-right after a shake would not be reversed; the rule says it should move left from right to middle.
If it came out middle or right, tilt-right after a shake would not be a leftward move, or the left boundary would not hold.

attack, rebuild fresh.final_rule: Start with the ball in the middle and a hidden polarity set to normal. Shake toggles the polarity but does not move the ball. In normal polarity, tilt left moves the ball one place left (staying left at the left edge), and tilt right moves it one place right (staying right at the right edge). In reversed polarity, tilt left moves the ball one place right, and tilt right moves it one place left, with the same edge-stay behavior.

rounds.rule: Start with the ball in the middle and the tray in normal mode. Tilt left moves the ball one step left in normal mode and one step right in reversed mode; tilt right moves it one step right in normal mode and one step left in reversed mode; shake toggles the mode without moving the ball, and the ball stays at an end if pushed further.

commitments.why: If this came out left or middle, it would show that shake does not reverse the tilt-left control, contradicting the hidden-mode rule.
If this came out right or middle, it would show that shake does not reverse the tilt-right control, contradicting the hidden-mode rule.
If this came out left, it would mean three shakes do not leave the system in reversed mode, so the parity/toggle rule is wrong.
This tests that a mid-sequence shake reverses the final tilt-left; if it came out left or middle, the reversal rule is wrong.
This tests that a mid-sequence shake reverses the final tilt-right; if it came out right or middle, the reversal rule is wrong.

rounds.rule: Start with the ball in the middle and the tray in normal mode. Shake toggles between normal and reversed; in normal mode tilt left moves one step left and tilt right moves one step right, while in reversed mode those directions swap, and the ball stays at an end if an action would push it further.

commitments.why: If it ended left or right, shake would not be toggling the direction back to normal, so the hidden-mode toggle rule would be wrong.
If it ended right or left, the second shake would not be restoring normal control, contradicting the toggle rule.
If it ended left or middle, three shakes would not leave the tray reversed, so the parity/toggle rule would fail.
If it ended middle or right, either shake did not reverse tilt-right or the ball did not stay at the left boundary, contradicting the rule.
If it ended middle or left, either shake did not reverse tilt-left or the ball did not stay at the right boundary, contradicting the rule.
